reason.stale_version: Release information changed. Check again before updating.
reason.update_not_checked: Check for an update before installing.

reason.updater_not_configured: This build has no configured update channel.
reason.platform_unsupported: Automatic updates are not supported on this system yet.
reason.endpoint_invalid: The update address failed its security check.
reason.manifest_invalid: The release manifest is incomplete or not for this computer.
reason.check_failed: The check could not finish. Other features are unaffected.
reason.default: Updates and model setup are independent; an update failure cannot lock the app.

yeschoyUpdate.safety: Every package must pass signature verification. Yeschoy stays open until download completes and never changes Codex, Claude, or other app settings during an update.

configuration.groupIntro: The same model comes in different price plans, and you're billed on the one you pick. The costs below all assume the same token mix.
configuration.groupsMissing: This model has no group pricing yet. It's billed on your account's default group, and you can connect it normally.
configuration.groupsEmptyHint: Pick a model to see its billing groups.
configuration.estimateExampleNote: A reference figure. Your actual cost moves with how you use it.
configuration.estimateFormula: About 0.69% new input + 99.14% cache reads + 0.17% output
configuration.estimateNote: Both sides use the same model, billing tier and usage. List prices convert at {{referenceFx}} and Yeschoy at {{siteFx}}, and the Yeschoy figure already includes the plan you picked. {{tiered}}Fixed reference rates — your bill is what counts. {{cacheNote}}
configuration.estimateTieredNote: The standard tier is used where there is one; otherwise the server's first tier. The range for other tiers is above.
configuration.estimateCacheFallbackNote: This model has no separate cache-read price, so the cached part is estimated conservatively at the input price.
configuration.estimateCacheExcludedNote: Cache writes billed separately are not included. What you pay follows the tier each request lands in.
configuration.estimateUnavailable: The current rules can't be converted into a token cost reliably, so no estimate is shown. Your website bill is what counts.
configuration.restoreFailed: The restore didn't finish and the record is kept. Close the target app and try again — nothing of yours will be overwritten by force.
configuration.tokenCleanupPending: The settings on this computer are restored. The remote app key has not been revoked yet — get online, sign in to the same account, and click "{{action}}" again to retry. The restored settings won't be touched.
configuration.tokenKept: The settings on this computer are restored. The remote app key was kept, as you chose: it still works and can still be billed. You can revoke it later on the website's token page.
configuration.restoredWithChanges: Everything restorable is back, and the edits you made afterwards are kept. Reopen the app for it to take effect.
configuration.restoredOriginal: The settings from before you connected are back. Reopen the app for it to take effect.
configuration.revokedLegacy: Yeschoy's setup is undone. The older version didn't save the original values, so pick the account or provider you want inside the app.
configuration.restoreError: Can't restore right now. Try again — the restore record is still on this computer.
configuration.introOriginal: Restore the model, provider and connection settings this app had before Yeschoy. Anything you changed afterwards is kept.
configuration.introLegacy: This connection came from an older version, which didn't save what was there before. Only the connection entries that still belong to Yeschoy can be undone; the original values can't be recovered.
configuration.noteNoUninstall: The app isn't uninstalled, and chat history isn't deleted.
configuration.noteIsolated: Other apps, website accounts and your balance aren't affected.
configuration.revokeOptionTitle: Also revoke this app's own key
configuration.revokeOnHint: Once revoked the key stops working immediately and can't be billed again.
configuration.revokeOffHint: If kept, the key still works and can still be billed. You can revoke it later on the website's token page.
configuration.outcomeTimeout: Timed out waiting for the model
configuration.outcomeUpstreamError: The model service didn't finish the request
configuration.outcomeStreamInterrupted: The reply stopped before it finished
configuration.outcomeUnknownModel: This model isn't in your model list yet
configuration.outcomePayloadTooLarge: The request is over this computer's safety limit
configuration.outcomeLocalBusy: This computer is handling another large request
configuration.advicePayloadTooLarge: A single request went over 200 MiB and wasn't sent upstream. Attach fewer files or images and try again.
configuration.adviceLocalBusy: To keep the desktop assistant responsive, it buffers only one large request at a time. Wait for the current one to finish and try again.
configuration.adviceUnauthorized: Check your account and whether it can use this model.
configuration.adviceRateLimited: Lots of requests, or a quota limit. Try again shortly and check your account.
configuration.adviceUnknownModel: Pick a model you've already configured, or add the new one to your list and update the connection.
configuration.adviceRetry: Try again first. If it keeps failing you can switch routes yourself — your model and billing group won't be changed for you.
configuration.emptyRequestState: No request from this app has come through Yeschoy yet. Send a message, then refresh here to confirm.
configuration.codexAccountNote: The official account Codex shows is a sign-in identity. It says nothing about which route this request took or who is billed. Only a record here means the request really went through Yeschoy.
configuration.attributionNote: These records come from the server's usage log, attributed by the tool's own key, and show the full model ID that was actually forwarded. They don't rely on the app's own label or on what the AI says about itself. Send a message, wait a few seconds, then refresh.
configuration.scanningHint: Reading the apps installed on this computer.
configuration.applyRunningHint: A connection is in progress. Controls come back once it finishes or is safely cancelled.
configuration.targetScanRetryHint: The app check didn't finish this time. Run it again — no settings are changed.
configuration.connectionReadRetryHint: Couldn't read the last connection status. Read it again — nothing existing is overwritten.
configuration.connectionReadingHint: Reading the connections already set up on this computer.
configuration.accountRefreshingHint: Refreshing your account, models and billing groups.
configuration.selectionSyncHint: Syncing the model selection for the current account.
configuration.chooseInstallHint: Several copies were found. The settings live in your user directory and apply to all of them; this only decides which one "Open" launches. The assistant preselects the one your terminal would run.
configuration.groupNotForThisApp: This price plan can't be used in {{app}}
configuration.missing: This app isn't on this computer. Install it, then check again.
configuration.unsupported: The app is here, but a component it needs to start is missing. Make sure it's fully installed, then check again.
configuration.scanFailed: Can't check this computer's apps right now. Try again.
configuration.verifying: Saving the settings securely and starting the local connection. No test message is sent…
configuration.verifyingCodex: Saving the Codex settings and key securely and preparing the local route. The app opens on its own when this is done…
configuration.verifyingDesktop: Saving the Claude Desktop settings securely and preparing the local connection. No waiting on a model reply.
configuration.verifyingDsh: Saving the DSH settings and starting the local workbench. No test message is sent…
configuration.verifyingWorkBuddy: Writing the models into WorkBuddy securely and reading them back to confirm. No billable test message is sent, and WorkBuddy isn't closed…
configuration.awaitingFirstUseBody: Open {{app}} and send anything. Only after the assistant sees that real request will it say the connection works — until then it only knows the settings were written correctly.
configuration.verifiedBody: {{app}} completed a real request with {{model}} through Yeschoy.
configuration.readyBody: {{app}}'s settings are saved and the local connection is ready. The real result shows up here after you first use it.
configuration.connectionFailed: The connection didn't complete and every change on this computer has been rolled back. Check again and retry.
configuration.configurationParseFailed: This app's existing config file can't be read — it may have been edited by hand, or it's damaged. Nothing was changed. Back the file up, fix the syntax (or delete it and let the app regenerate it), then try connecting again.
configuration.configurationReadFailed: Can't read this app's config file. Another program may have it open, or there's no permission to read it. Close the app and try again; if the home screen shows settings waiting to be restored, restore them first.
configuration.configurationWriteFailed: Can't write this app's config file, and the original settings are back. Usually antivirus or the app itself is holding the file, or the disk is full. Close them and try again.
configuration.configurationReadbackFailed: The settings were written and then changed back by another program, so the originals are restored. Usually antivirus or a cloud-sync folder is watching this file. Allow-list it or pause syncing, then try again.
configuration.credentialHelperFailed: Codex couldn't read the tool key from the system's secure storage, so the settings are restored. Quit Yeschoy, open it again, and retry.
configuration.authenticationFailed: The route you picked didn't accept the tool key, so the settings are restored. Refresh your account and try again.
configuration.endpointUnavailable: The route you picked can't reach this model's endpoint right now, so the settings are restored. Switch routes or try again later.
configuration.providerTimedOut: The route you picked timed out, so the settings are restored. Switch routes or try again later.
configuration.providerBusy: This model is busy right now, so the settings are restored. Try again shortly or pick another model.
configuration.modelRequestRejected: The model you picked didn't accept the test request, so the settings are restored. Refresh the model list and pick again.
configuration.invalidProviderResponse: The route returned a model reply we couldn't read, so the settings are restored. Try again later.
configuration.desktopTimedOut: No test message arrived from Claude Desktop, so the connection isn't confirmed and the changes on this computer are rolled back.
configuration.missingDuringSetup: The app you picked is no longer there. Check again.
configuration.selectionRequired: Several installs were found. Pick the one to use.
configuration.secureStoreFailed: The system's secure storage isn't available. Unlock your keychain or credential manager, check this computer's connection status, then try again.
configuration.externalOverride: Another setup already owns this app's config directory, so nothing of yours was touched. Launch it with "Open" from here instead, or pick an install that isn't already taken.
configuration.unsupportedProfile: The way this app runs can't be configured automatically yet. Nothing was changed.
configuration.launchFailed: The settings were rolled back because the app didn't start. Make sure it opens by hand.
configuration.builderIntro: Pick your models, compare group prices, then connect in one go. The network route is chosen separately.
configuration.lineQuestion: Pick by where you are. It doesn't change the price.
configuration.finishHint: Writes the app's settings securely and reads them back. No billable test message is sent.
configuration.endpointReferenceNote: A documentation value. What counts is the endpoint written into the app's settings.
configuration.surfaceCodexDesktop: Codex inside the ChatGPT desktop app
configuration.surfaceWorkBuddy: Tencent's AI assistant for work and development
configuration.lifecycleDesktopRestart: If {{name}} is running, updating the connection asks you to save first. Once you confirm, the assistant asks the app to quit normally, writes the settings and reopens it. On Windows, if only a background process is left, only the process at this install path is ended.
configuration.lifecycleBrowserLaunch: Updating the connection saves the DSH config. "Open" only starts the local service and opens it in your browser — no model test message is sent.
configuration.lifecycleTerminalSession: Updating the connection doesn't close the command-line session you're in. New settings apply to newly opened sessions.
configuration.lifecycleHotReload: WorkBuddy picks up the updated model list on its own — nothing to close or restart. Conversations already open may keep their old model, so start a new one and pick a Yeschoy model in the model picker.
configuration.retryRollbackFailed: Something went wrong while rolling back the last unfinished setup, and part of it isn't restored yet. Click "Fix and retry" — you don't need to edit any config by hand.
configuration.retryCredentialRestore: The key settings weren't restored during the automatic rollback. Unlock your system keychain or credential manager, then click "Fix and retry" — you don't need to edit any config by hand.
configuration.retryRecoveryPending: Another connect or restore is running. This app wasn't changed. Try again shortly; if it keeps happening, use "Restore original settings".
configuration.readyTerminal: {{app}}'s settings and local connection are ready. Running command-line sessions aren't interrupted — open a new one, or click "Open in terminal". The result of the first real request shows up under "Recent connection results".
configuration.readyCodex: {{app}}'s settings and the Yeschoy local route are ready. {{favorites}}Codex may still show your official sign-in account; that's an identity, not proof that requests are billed officially. The result of the first real request shows up under "Recent requests through Yeschoy" — seeing the full model ID is what tells you the request really went through Yeschoy.
configuration.favoritesConfigured: Your models were set up along with it.
configuration.readyDefault: {{app}}'s settings and local connection are ready. {{favorites}}Use the app as usual; the result of the first real request shows up under "Recent connection results".
configuration.readyWorkBuddy: The models are in WorkBuddy. {{favorites}}No restart needed — start a new conversation and pick a Yeschoy model in the model picker. Existing conversations aren't switched over. WorkBuddy's config format requires the key to sit directly in ~/.workbuddy/models.json (set readable only by you) — keep that file out of synced cloud folders, and don't send it to anyone.
configuration.restartBlocked: The system couldn't close {{app}}, so nothing was changed. Check that no system dialog is in the way, or quit it yourself and try again.
configuration.appRunning: {{app}} is running. Save anything unfinished, then confirm to let the assistant close and reopen it. On Windows, if only a background process is left, only the process at the recognized install path is ended.
configuration.launchStateUnavailable: Can't safely confirm whether the app is running, so nothing was changed. Quit the app yourself and try again.
configuration.launchAccessDenied: The settings are saved, but the system blocked opening the app. Open it from your system menu.
configuration.launchTargetChanged: The settings are saved, but the app's install location just changed. Check apps again, then open it yourself.
configuration.launchStoreApp: The settings are saved, but this store app can't be opened automatically right now. Open it once from the Start menu.
configuration.launchNotOpened: The settings are saved, but the app didn't open on its own. Open it yourself — no need to connect again.
configuration.launchStartFailed: The settings are saved, but the app didn't start. Check that it's still where it was and opens by hand — no need to connect again.
configuration.launchUnconfirmed: The settings are saved, but we couldn't confirm the app started. Take a look at whether it opened — no need to connect again.
configuration.claudeLoginBlockLabel: Deal with the claude.ai sign-in first
configuration.claudeLoginBlockHint: Claude Code is still signed in to claude.ai, which overrides the Yeschoy connection.
configuration.claudeLoginDialogTitle: Claude Code is still signed in to claude.ai
configuration.claudeLoginDialogMessage: With both sign-ins present, Claude Code uses the claude.ai one and the Yeschoy connection won't take effect. The assistant can put the claude.ai sign-in aside and hand it back untouched later under "Restore original settings" — nothing is lost. Your system will ask once whether Yeschoy may use information in your keychain; that prompt is for this. Allow it.
configuration.claudeLoginNotReleased: The system didn't allow keychain access, so the claude.ai sign-in wasn't put aside. Nothing was connected and no settings changed. Try again and choose "Allow" when your system asks.
configuration.claudeLoginTakeoverFailed: Couldn't put the claude.ai sign-in aside. Nothing was connected and no settings changed. You can try again; if it keeps failing, run claude /logout in Claude Code and then connect.
configuration.launchTerminalFailed: The settings are saved, but a terminal window couldn't be opened. Open a terminal yourself and start it there — no need to connect again.
configuration.launchTerminalUnavailable: The settings are saved, but no usable terminal program was found. On macOS check that Terminal is still there; on Windows check that the system directory is reachable. No need to connect again.
configuration.launchWorkspaceUnavailable: The settings are saved, but the working folder isn't usable — it may have been moved or deleted, or there's no permission to write there. Pick another working folder and open it again.
configuration.launchTargetInvalid: The settings are saved, but this app's install path can't be used (not an absolute path, or it contains special characters). Install it somewhere ordinary and check apps again.
configuration.launchTargetMissing: The settings are saved, but this app's executable wasn't found — it may have been moved or uninstalled. Check apps again.
configuration.launchExitFailed: The settings are saved, but this app didn't quit, and the new settings only apply after it reopens. Quit it yourself, then start it with "Open".
configuration.launchWaitFailed: The settings are saved, but we couldn't confirm this app had quit. Make sure it's closed, then start it with "Open".
configuration.homeUnavailable: Can't read the current user's home directory, so nothing was changed. Make sure your account's user folder is reachable and try again.
configuration.codexHistoryConflict: The last Codex history cleanup hasn't finished, so this one didn't continue and no settings changed. Your conversations are safe. Close Codex and try again.
configuration.codexHistoryFailed: Couldn't sort out who owns the Codex conversation history, so the settings are restored. Your conversations are safe and still where they were. Close Codex and try again.
configuration.codexHistoryRecoveryFailed: Sorting out the Codex history failed, and the rollback didn't finish either. Nothing was deleted, but some conversations may not appear in Codex's resume list for now. Don't start a new conversation yet — go back to the connection settings and run "Restore original settings".
configuration.verifyStartFailed: The app didn't start, so the connection settings are restored. Make sure it's fully installed and opens by hand.
configuration.verifyTimedOut: The app's connection test timed out, so the connection settings are restored. Try again later.
configuration.verifyReadFailed: Couldn't read the app's test result, so the connection settings are restored. Reopen the assistant and try again.
configuration.verifyInvalidReply: The app didn't produce a valid model reply, so the connection settings are restored. Check the model and group you picked, then try again.
configuration.bridgeUnavailable: The Yeschoy local gateway wasn't ready in time, so the connection settings are restored. Reopen the Yeschoy assistant and try again.
configuration.bridgeAuthFailed: The Yeschoy local gateway's security token didn't match, so the connection settings are restored. Connect again and the assistant will issue a new one.
configuration.bridgeCatalogInvalid: The Yeschoy local gateway didn't load the full model list, so the connection settings are restored. Check your models and try again.
configuration.installConfirmRequired: The install finished, but your current selection needs confirming again. Check the account and model, then connect — the app's settings weren't changed this time.
configuration.assistantShuttingDown: The assistant is quitting, so this connection stopped. Anything already written is restored first.
configuration.activationCancelled: This connection was cancelled. If writing had already started, the original settings were restored first.
configuration.activationTimedOut: The connection waited more than 90 seconds. The page is usable again and the background work was told to cancel safely. Check the connection status first; if it still says in progress, wait a moment rather than submitting again.
configuration.activationAlreadyRunning: A connection is already finishing up safely. Wait a moment and try again — nothing was submitted twice.
configuration.accountChanged: The account changed, so this connection stopped. Confirm the current account and connect again.
configuration.invalidResponseResult: Can't confirm the result right now. Check this computer's connection status first rather than submitting again.
configuration.recoveryStorageUnavailable: Can't save the original settings safely, so this app wasn't changed. Make sure your system keychain or credential manager is available and try again.
configuration.recoveryReceiptFailed: The connection record wasn't fully saved. Check the local state, restore, and try again.
configuration.progressCheckingApp: Checking the app and its original settings…
configuration.progressSecuringAccess: Creating a key limited to the models you picked…
configuration.progressRestoring: Didn't finish — restoring the original settings…
configuration.versionUnreadNote: Version not read — you can still try connecting
configuration.signInHint: Sign in to scan this computer's apps and connect in one click.
configuration.refreshAccountHint: Your account data didn't update, so prices and groups may be stale. Fetch it again here.
configuration.installHint: This app isn't on this computer yet. The assistant installs it first, then connects.
configuration.installUnavailableHint: This app wasn't detected on this computer. Install it, then check again here — nothing is changed.
configuration.updateFirstHint: The version found can't be connected yet. Update the app, then check again here.
configuration.selectInstallationHint: There are several install locations on this computer. Pick one above first.
configuration.restartAppHint: The settings haven't been written. This app is running — confirm here once you've saved, and the assistant will close and reopen it.
configuration.viewAccountRelogin: Open account and sign in again
configuration.recheckApp: Check the app and connection again
configuration.accountStaleTitle: Account data isn't up to date
configuration.accountStaleBody: What you see are last time's models and prices. Refresh before connecting — apps you've already connected still open from "My apps".
configuration.missingModelSuffix: isn't available right now. Pick another one — nothing is swapped in for you.
configuration.billingCardHint: Choose price and source. The network route stays as it is.
configuration.missingGroupTitle: That billing group is no longer available
configuration.missingGroupBody: isn't among the groups this model currently offers. Pick again above — the price may differ, and nothing is switched for you.
configuration.favoriteModelsIntro: Once connected you can switch between these models inside the app, each with its own billing group.
configuration.bindingUnavailable: Not available — pick again or remove
configuration.favoriteModelsEmpty: Add one model to start; you can add more any time.
configuration.pendingModelEditNote: The model you picked below isn't in the list yet. Click "{{action}}", then confirm the connection.
configuration.favoriteModelsNote: The dot on the left marks the default. After adding a model, changing the default or switching a group, come back and update the connection once.
configuration.lineIntro: Mainland optimized suits networks in mainland China; Global accelerated goes through Cloudflare and is the one to try from elsewhere. The route only affects how you connect — billing groups and multipliers stay the same.
configuration.configuredSummary: These settings are saved. Switch models day to day inside the app; when you change this list, update the connection again.
configuration.modelSetNote: Every model is configured securely when you connect. Each one's real connection result appears after its first use.
configuration.lifecycleNotePrefix: Opening the app doesn't change any settings.
configuration.backgroundNote: Keep the Yeschoy assistant running while you work. Closing the window can leave it running in the background; quitting entirely cuts the model connection. It never locks your app, and you can restore the original settings at any time.
configuration.progressNote: Progress shows up here. The rest of the page still works — just don't click connect again.
configuration.staleContextPrefix: What was handled just now was the account
configuration.staleContextSuffix: . Your current selection hasn't been applied.
configuration.restartDialogMessage:
This app is running. Save whatever you're editing first.

After you continue you don't need to quit it yourself: the Yeschoy assistant asks it to quit normally, writes the settings, then reopens it. On Windows, if only a background process is left, only the process at the recognized install path is ended — nothing is killed by name. If the system still blocks the quit, no settings are changed.

stage.awaiting_system_confirmation: Finish the install in the system window

reason.diskFull: Not enough space on this computer. Free some up and try again — nothing you already have is deleted.
reason.permissionDenied: The system won't allow writing to the install location right now. Use the official install instead, then come back and check.
reason.sourceChallenge: The official site wants a browser check right now. Finish the install on its page, then come back and check.
reason.packageRejected: The package didn't pass its check, so the install stopped. Download it again, or use the official install.
reason.securityBlocked: The system hasn't allowed the install. Check the system prompt or the official instructions — you don't need to turn off any security.
reason.installerUnavailable: Couldn't open or confirm the system installer. Check Windows App Installer and any system prompt, or use the official install.
reason.notDetected: The installed app hasn't been found yet. Finish the install in the system window, then check below.
reason.handoffDismissed: Yeschoy's install guide has ended. The Windows install is not cancelled. You can install something else, or come back and check once it's done.
reason.cacheFull: Two packages that may still be in use are being kept, so no other version can be downloaded for now. Use the official install and come back to check — nothing possibly still in use is deleted.
reason.locationConflict: Something with the same name is already at the install location, and we can't confirm it's this app. It wasn't replaced. Use the official install to pick another location, then come back and check.
reason.alreadyInstalled: This app is already on your computer — no need to reinstall. Check again and you can pick a model and connect.
reason.mountCleanupPending: The app is kept, but the install disk hasn't been ejected. Eject it in Finder, then check the app again.
reason.unconfirmed: Can't confirm where the app is installed right now. Check the app again — nothing existing was deleted or replaced.
reason.unknown: The download or install didn't finish. You can try again — what's already downloaded is kept where possible, and nothing you have is deleted.

source.mirror: Source: Yeschoy's mainland mirror · vendor signature checked before installing
source.official: Source: the vendor's own site · vendor signature checked before installing
source.none: Yeschoy's mainland mirror is used first, falling back to the vendor's own site.

installation.leadOther: Finish the current install before starting another.
installation.leadGuided: Follow the official steps. Once it's installed, Yeschoy connects the model for you.
installation.leadAuto: The right package is picked for you — no version hunting, no commands.
installation.awaitingPublisher: Check that the publisher is {{publisher}}. If it offers to reinstall or replace, cancel — come back and connect the app you already have.
installation.awaitingSignature: The system checks the package's signature. Closing Yeschoy doesn't cancel that system window.
installation.installedNote: Installing the app and connecting a model are two steps. It only says connected once a real result comes back.
installation.unsupportedCodexArm: The official Codex package is for Apple-silicon Macs. On this computer you can start with Claude; a Codex you already installed can still be checked and connected.
installation.unsupportedGeneric: There's no automatic package for this computer yet. Check the official support list, or pick another app.
installation.selectionChanged: Your selection changed. The install can carry on — once it's done, confirm the model before you connect.
installation.progressStale: The install progress hasn't updated. Check it rather than starting the install again.
installation.endGuide: End this guide (the Windows install continues)
installation.footNoteConnect: Once installed, the model you picked is connected. No billable test message is sent.
installation.footNoteSignIn: You can install first, then sign in to Yeschoy, pick a model and connect.
installation.noSignInNeeded: Installing and checking work without signing in. Sign in to Yeschoy afterwards to pick a model and connect.

status.opened: The open request was sent. Nothing is reconfigured and no test message is sent.
status.not_connected: The connection details are gone. Connect again.
status.settings_changed: This app's connection settings changed, and your edits weren't overwritten. Adjust the connection, or restore the original settings.
status.recovery_pending: The last connection didn't finish. Go to the connection settings and connect again — the assistant rolls back what was left over first, with no config editing on your part.
status.secure_storage_unavailable: Can't read the connection details the system saved. Unlock your keychain or credential manager and try again.
status.tool_not_found: No app was found to launch. Check the install and try again.
status.launch_failed: Couldn't open the app or a terminal. Check that it opens by hand and isn't blocked by the system, then check again.
status.busy: Another app operation is still running. Try again once it's done.

launchReason.terminal_launch_failed: Couldn't open a terminal window. The connection settings are untouched — open a terminal yourself and start it there, or try again.
launchReason.terminal_unavailable: No usable terminal program was found. On macOS check that Terminal is still there; on Windows check that the system directory is reachable. The connection settings are untouched.
launchReason.workspace_unavailable: The working folder isn't usable — it may have been moved or deleted, or there's no permission to write there. Pick another one in the connection settings.
launchReason.invalid_launch_target: This app's install path can't be used (not an absolute path, or it contains special characters). Install it somewhere ordinary and check the app again.
launchReason.launch_target_missing: This app's executable wasn't found — it may have been moved or uninstalled. Check the app again.
launchReason.desktop_launch_start_failed: This app didn't start. Check that it's still where it was and that it opens by hand.
launchReason.desktop_launch_exit_failed: This app didn't quit, and the new settings only apply after it reopens. Quit it yourself and try again.
launchReason.desktop_launch_wait_failed: Couldn't confirm this app had quit. Make sure it's closed and try again.
launchReason.desktop_launch_access_denied: The system blocked this launch. Allow it under System Settings → Privacy & Security, or open it by hand once.
launchReason.desktop_start_unconfirmed: Couldn't confirm whether this app opened. Take a look — the connection settings are untouched.
launchReason.desktop_launch_target_changed: This app's install location just changed. Check the app again, then open it.

openConnection.openedTerminal: A terminal was requested — use it in the new window. Nothing is reconfigured and no test message is sent.
openConnection.unconfirmedError: Can't confirm the result right now. You can try again — the app wasn't reconfigured.
openConnection.unconfirmedTimeout: Timed out waiting for the app, and the page is usable again. It may still open shortly; if it doesn't, try again. The connection settings weren't modified.
openConnection.dialogIntro: {{name}} runs in a terminal — there is no separate desktop window. Click “Open in terminal” and the assistant starts it for you; you can also run it from a terminal in your project folder:
openConnection.dialogSaved: The model and connection details are saved in the app, so there's no key to copy. Sessions already open may keep the old settings — start a new one.
openConnection.dialogBackground: Keep the Yeschoy assistant running while you use it.

quit.settingsBody: When you close the window you can keep it running in the background, or restore the original settings and quit. You can also quit and leave the connections in place.
quit.unknownAffected: Can't confirm which apps need the assistant running. Quitting may interrupt a connection in use. No settings are deleted.
quit.affectedIntro: These apps' connections need the assistant running, and will be interrupted when you quit:
quit.affectedHint: Choose “Keep running” if you want to carry on. Once you quit, reopen the assistant and continue from the app card — there is nothing to reconnect.
quit.noneAffected: Quitting puts back the settings each app had before you connected. App settings and chat history are never deleted, and you can connect again at any time.
quit.detailClose: The assistant asks Codex and Claude to close normally. It never force-quits and never reopens them for you — save your work first. Command-line apps pick up the settings the next time they start.
quit.detailKeep: Settings you changed yourself and your chat history are kept, and the remote key isn't revoked. Reopen those apps afterwards and they go back to your own official account or provider.
quit.detailBackground: “Keep running” only minimises the window and holds the connections. It doesn't quit the assistant.
quit.restoreFailedIntro: These apps couldn't be restored, so the assistant hasn't quit:
quit.restoreFailedHint: Save and close the apps, make sure the system's secure storage is available, then try again. Connections made by an older version have no original settings to restore. Restores that succeeded are not undone — you can also quit and leave the rest in place.
quit.restoringSettings: Closing the desktop apps normally and restoring their settings. Nothing is force-quit. Deal with any save prompt first; the assistant quits once this is done.
quit.finishingOperation: Finishing the current connection or account operation so nothing ends up half-written. The assistant quits on its own once it's safe — you can dismiss this or wait in the background.
quit.exiting: Safely finishing up and closing the assistant's background connections. No other app is force-closed.
quit.errorBackground: Can't move to the background right now. Try again.
quit.errorExit: Can't confirm the quit status right now. Try again — nothing being saved is interrupted by force.

savings.comparisonLabel: Cost comparison over the same records
savings.receiptSummary: How is the saving worked out?
savings.counts: Of the last {{scanned}} charges, {{included}} were compared and {{excluded}} were left out. This is not a running total or a monthly figure.
savings.formulaOfficial: Each record's billed units ÷ that record's multiplier × the current reference rate {{rate}}, summed
savings.formulaSite: The same billed units × the current site price factor {{rate}}, summed
savings.emptyRecords: No charges yet. Use a model and they'll show up here.
savings.noComparable: The last {{count}} records don't have complete billing data to compare against yet.
savings.unavailable: Couldn't get the full bill or price settings. Refresh your account and try again.
savings.neverZero: Missing data is never counted as a saving of zero.
savings.basisNote: Billed units come from the actual charge divided by the site's credit unit. A record's own multiplier is used where there is one, otherwise the group's. Cache is already part of the actual charge — no fixed cache ratio is assumed.
savings.excludedNote: Records with no basis, plan-based usage and special surcharges are left out. Figures are estimated from the list prices the site maintains and its current price settings. They are not an actual list-price bill, and not the same as a top-up cash discount. The conversion rate is not a market exchange rate.
savings.noteEmpty: Shows up once you have charges

connectionError.connection_partial_unavailable: Some apps' connection settings couldn't be read. The rest are still shown. Try again — if it keeps happening, send us the diagnostic id below.
connectionError.connection_inspect_timed_out: Timed out reading the connection status. System credentials or local settings may still be loading. Try again shortly.
connectionError.connection_restore_timed_out: The restore hasn't reported back yet. Read the status again to check rather than restoring twice.
connectionError.connection_operation_busy: Another connect or restore is running. Try again once it's done.
connectionError.assistant_shutting_down: The assistant is quitting. Reopen it and check again.
connectionError.invalid_connection_response: The connection status came back in a shape we can't read. Try again — if it keeps happening, send us the diagnostic id below.
connectionError.connection_inspection_failed: Reading this computer's state didn't finish. Try again.
connectionError.connection_call_failed: Can't read the connection status right now. Try again.

connectionNotice.stale: What's below is the last confirmed result, not this one. Nothing is overwritten with a default.
connectionNotice.unconfirmed: The connection status isn't confirmed. That doesn't mean the app isn't connected, and nothing is overwritten with a default.

advancedDetails.folderLaunch: (opened as a folder, no fixed file)

modelPicker.searchPlaceholder: Search by name or ID, e.g. GPT 6
